title: "C05 Proportional Control"
description: "Relate controller output to present error and investigate proportional gain."

execute: {enabled: false}

Proportional control makes the command proportional to present error.

$$u=K_Pe$$

For $K_P=20\%/{}^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $e=2.0^\circ\mathrm{C}$, the command is $40\%$ before applying output limits.

Higher proportional gain often gives a faster response and smaller steady-state error. Excessive gain can produce overshoot or oscillation.

## Evidence table

| Gain | Rise time | Overshoot | Steady-state error | Stability |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--|
| low | | | | |
| medium | | | | |
| high | | | | |

Choose one gain and defend the choice using the graph rather than the gain number alone.
